final_answer: The Rosetta Stone was a pivotal artifact that enabled the decipherment of Egyptian hieroglyphs, unlocking access to ancient Egyptian history, culture, and language. It contained the same text in three scripts: Ancient Greek, Demotic, and hieroglyphs. Since Greek was already understood, scholars could compare the scripts to identify phonetic and symbolic meanings in hieroglyphs. Jean-François Champollion, a French scholar, used this method to decode hieroglyphs in the early 19th century, revealing that they combined logographic and phonetic elements. This breakthrough transformed Egyptology, allowing the study of ancient Egyptian texts and reshaping understanding of the civilization.
